_comment: Supervisor routing mapping (P10b). A manager asks one question in their own words; this file declares which section agent answers which kind of question. Copy the section list into config/integrations.json as the 'supervisor' block under the tenant key, then declare the same sections through PUT /{tenant}/supervisor/{section} so the change is audited and owner-only. This file is the readable copy of that mapping, not a secret store.
_note_authority: The target agent runs with ITS OWN policy. The supervisor's authority is never inherited: a supervisor that cannot read the CRM cannot reach the CRM by routing to an agent that can. Authority flows to the executor, not to the asker.
_note_chain: Chains are bounded. max_hops defaults to 1 (a single delegation) and is counted from the ledger, so it survives a restart. Routing to an agent that is itself a router is refused by default, which is what stops supervisor -> supervisor -> ...
_note_keywords: Keywords are matched literally and case-folded, longest first, then declaration order. They are deliberately not regular expressions: an operator writes a word, and a typo cannot silently widen a match. A question that matches no section is REFUSED by name rather than sent to a default agent, because the wrong agent answering a payroll question is worse than no answer.
_note_limits: A section whose agent has lost its policy is skipped rather than offered, so routing can never create a run the target itself could not authorise.
